objective: Synthesize randomized-trial evidence for remote blood-pressure monitoring in adults with hypertension.

questions.text: What is the effect of remote monitoring on systolic blood pressure at approximately six months?

inputs.description: Deduplicated records from the prespecified bibliographic and trial-registry searches.

design.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials

units.description: Independent randomized comparison, linked across multiple reports when necessary.
Publication or registry record nested within a study.

outcomes.definition: Between-group mean difference in systolic blood pressure nearest six months.

analysis_sets.definition: Randomized trials in eligible adults comparing remote monitoring with usual care and reporting the primary outcome.

contrasts.definition: Remote blood-pressure monitoring compared with usual care.

restrictions: Do not treat publication count as independent study count.

steps.method: Prespecified database and registry searches with duplicate independent screening.

steps.purpose: Extract outcomes, assess bias, synthesize effects, and rate certainty.
steps.method: Duplicate extraction, domain-level risk-of-bias assessment, random-effects synthesis, and certainty grading.

required_outputs.description: Effect estimates, heterogeneity, risk of bias, and certainty for the primary outcome.

validation.criterion: Multiple reports from the same trial are linked to one study before synthesis.
